:::{#thm-similar-eigenvalues}
#### Similar matrices have the same eigenvalues

If $\matr{B} = \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P}$ (@def-similar),
then $\vecf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $\matr{A}$ for $\lambda$
exactly when $\matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v}$ is an eigenvector of $\matr{B}$ for $\lambda$.
So $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$ have the same eigenvalues.

:::

::: proof

If $\matr{A} \vecf{v} = \lambda \vecf{v}$ with $\vecf{v} \ne \vzero$, let $\vecf{w} = \matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v}$. Then

$$
\ba
\matr{B} \vecf{w}
&= (\matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \matr{P})\,(\matr{P}^{-1} \vecf{v})
&& \text{(substitute } \matr{B} \text{ and } \vecf{w} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A}\,(\matr{P} \matr{P}^{-1})\,\vecf{v}
&& \text{(@thm-matmul-assoc)}
\\
&= \matr{P}^{-1} \matr{A} \vecf{v}
&& \text{(@def-matrix-inverse, @thm-identity)}
\\
&= \matr{P}^{-1}\,(\lambda \vecf{v})
&& \text{(eigenvector)}
\\
&= \lambda\,\vecf{w},
&& \text{(@thm-scalar-matmul)}
\ea
$$

and $\vecf{w} \ne \vzero$, since $\matr{P}^{-1}$ is invertible and so has null space $\cb{\vzero}$
(@thm-invertible-rank).
For the converse, $\matr{A} = \matr{P} \matr{B} \matr{P}^{-1} = (\matr{P}^{-1})^{-1} \matr{B}\,\matr{P}^{-1}$,
so the same argument with the roles of $\matr{A}$ and $\matr{B}$ exchanged
sends an eigenvector $\vecf{w}$ of $\matr{B}$ to the eigenvector $\matr{P} \vecf{w}$ of $\matr{A}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-similar-eigenvalues}
#### Eigenvectors carried across a similarity

In @exm-similar, $\matr{B} = \operatorname{diag}(3, 1)$ has eigenvectors $(1, 0)$ for $3$ and $(0, 1)$ for $1$.
$\matr{P}\,(1, 0) = (1, 1)$ and $\matr{P}\,(0, 1) = (1, -1)$
are the eigenvectors of $\matr{A}$ for $3$ and $1$ found in @exm-eigenvalue.

:::
